findings.claim: The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the class is defined at import time. Every AssignmentSource in a process therefore gets the module-import or worker-start time, not its own creation or queue time, and that stale value is serialised into every sync_assignee_outbound task through to_dict(). Nothing reads `queued` today, but any future staleness or loop check built on it would silently break. Fix: field(default_factory=timezone.now), or drop the unused field.
findings.evidence: Python evaluates dataclass defaults once, at class creation. superpowers ran a repro against the patched file with a stubbed django.utils.timezone: two instances built 1.5 s apart got identical timestamps (2026-11-14 08:29:00.514144+00:00) and the script raised AssertionError. ponytail gave a plain-Python equivalent that shows the same behaviour. open-code-review proposed a freeze_time test asserting a.queued != b.queued, which was reasoned and not run. The existing test_to_dict (test_assignment_source.py:29-38) only asserts queued is not None, so it passes despite the bug. Severity was Important from open-code-review and superpowers and Minor from ponytail; normalised to Important. mattpocock raised it under 'Outside my axes'.
findings.reason: Four seats agree, and a reproduction exists that fails on the pinned code. Red test: a per-instance `queued` test (open-code-review's freeze_time test) must fail on the pinned code before the fix and stay in the suite. The smallest fix is field(default_factory=timezone.now). ponytail's alternative, deleting the unused field, is also acceptable. Current runtime impact is nil because nothing reads `queued`.

findings.claim: The abstract sync_status_outbound gains an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller passes and no implementation reads. tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 still calls should_sync("outbound_status") with no source, so status-sync loops get no protection even though the signature implies they do. ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound (example/integration.py:161) has no **kwargs, so it would raise TypeError once a caller passed the argument. The abstract contract is inconsistent: sync_assignee_outbound, the method that actually receives the source, does not declare the parameter.
findings.evidence: All four seats grep'd and found no call site passing assignment_source to sync_status_outbound. Concrete implementations do not declare it (jira:990, jira_server:1090, vsts:266, example:161). The tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 call has no source. Nothing fails at runtime today.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Smallest change: revert to `def sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id, **kwargs):`. That removes the dead parameter and the false promise of status-loop protection. Whether status-sync cycles were in scope cannot be settled without a spec, so extending protection to status sync is not done here. No red test is required at Minor severity.

findings.claim: from_dict swallows TypeError and ValueError and returns None with no log or metric. should_sync then treats the call as having no source and syncs, so a malformed payload silently fails open into the cycle this change is meant to prevent.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code at assignment_source.py:31-35 and should_sync. Counterpoints from other seats: ponytail notes the only producer is to_dict and the fallback is the pre-patch behaviour, a safe degradation. open-code-review confirms from_dict({}) returns None as designed. Neither disproves the lack of observability.
findings.reason: Appendix: only two seats raised it, so it is not fixed in this loop. ponytail: consider a log or metric on the None path if payload provenance ever widens beyond to_dict.

findings.claim: from_dict does not type-check `queued` on the way back in. Under pickle it stays a datetime, but if the Celery serializer became JSON it would come back as a str.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. Celery uses pickle here (conf/server.py:739, CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"), so it is harmless today.
findings.reason: Appendix: single seat, and harmless under the current pickle serializer. ponytail: revisit if the task serializer changes.

findings.claim: The loop guard compares integration IDs, not external issue IDs. If a group is linked to two external issues on the same integration install (for example Jira issues A and B), an inbound reassignment on A is no longer pushed to B. Before this patch it was, so a sync that was not part of any loop is now silently dropped.
findings.evidence: Reasoned: sync_group_assignee_outbound queues one task per linked external issue, and each task's should_sync("outbound_assignee", source) returns False whenever source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id, regardless of external issue. No test covers this case, and it may be intended.
findings.reason: Appendix: single seat, and without a spec it is unclear whether this is intended. ponytail: settle with a test linking two external issues on one integration and asserting the non-source issue still receives the sync.

findings.claim: The new task keyword assignment_source_dict and its sender (utils/sync.py:136-144) ship in the same deploy. During a rolling deploy, an old worker that receives a task with assignment_source_dict= raises TypeError (unexpected keyword) and that assignee sync is lost. Sentry's practice is to ship the task parameter, with a default, one deploy before any caller sends it.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. mattpocock's 'deploy-safe' check covers only the other direction: old-format tasks reaching new workers succeed because the kwarg defaults to None. That does not disprove new-format tasks reaching old workers. The practice is Sentry external developer guidance and is not documented in this repo.
findings.reason: Appendix: single seat. Not disproved by the other reports. ponytail: confirm whether a two-phase deploy is needed before release.

coverage: No files were skipped: every seat reviewed all 7 files in the patch. open-code-review's tool excluded the two test files by default_path, but the seat reviewed them manually under the override. The gate was not run (benchmark mode), so this review is unanchored: no build, test, lint or mypy results back any finding. The only executed evidence is superpowers' standalone repro for assignment_source.py:18 (with a stubbed django.utils.timezone) and ponytail's plain-Python equivalent. Spec axis: did not run, no spec. Seats judged against the inferred intent from the commit title 'fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles'. Standards axis: only partly ran. The repo documents no coding standards locally (.github/CONTRIBUTING.md links to external docs.sentry.io/internal, which no seat checked), so mattpocock used enforced in-repo conventions instead: holds_bad_pickle_object, the services/ layout, and the mypy config. No reviewer from another model family took a correctness seat. Rejections: none. No seat report disproves another's finding, so no verifier was needed.
